data: First soft landing on Mars; 14.5 s of surface transmission
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

The first soft landing on Mars (December 1971). Began transmitting what would have been a surface image, but contact was lost after 14.5 seconds leaving only a featureless grey frame. The global dust storm raging across the planet may have contributed to the early transmission loss.
First spacecraft to soft-land on Mars
The Soviet / Russian heavy-lift workhorse 1967-2012 — Salyut, Mir, Venera, Vega, Luna sample-return
First human-made object to reach Mars surface; lander crashed (1971)
First soft landing on another planet and first to transmit data from another planet's surface (Venus, 1970)
Soviet 1973 Mars lander — first descent telemetry from Mars atmosphere (224 s, mostly corrupted)
First soft landing on another world
Last successful Soviet Moon mission — returned 170 g of Mare Crisium regolith 1976-08-22; last lunar sample return until Chang'e 5

First soft landing on Mars. The lander touched down successfully and began transmitting data — for roughly 14.5 seconds. A planet-wide dust storm at the time of arrival is the leading explanation for the silence that followed. Despite the brevity, Mars 3 proved a Martian soft landing was possible: a foundational engineering result built on by every Mars lander since.
